M1 l Reflective Essay  
One of the most influential people in my life who inspired me to take my current course is 
my Kuya . When we were younger and living in Balibago, I often accompanied him to co mputer 
shops, where I discovered video games. What started as simple enj oyment slowly turned into 
curiosity about how computers worked, which eventually led me to pursue a course related to 
technology. As a teen entering her twenties , the value that I take  from Eastern perspectives on the 
self, particularly the Confucian principle of considering others before oneself. His respectful way 
of treating people and his sense of responsibility shaped how I interact with others. I see this 
reflected in my own belief of “ Don’t do unto others what you don’t want done unto you” showing 
how relational and moral values continue to guide my choices.  
 
As I grew older, I also developed traits influenced by Western perspectives, especially the idea of 
independence and individualism. I enjoy doing things on my own, making my own de cisions, and 
being responsible for my personal growth. This habit reflects the Western view of the self as 
independent and self -directed. While Eastern culture emphasizes family and community, my 
preference for independence sometimes puts me in between these two perspectives. There are 
moments when I struggle to balance being self -reliant while still valuing close family ties, but this 
combination ultimately shapes my identity. It allows me to value personal freedom without losing 
respect for relationships and shared responsibilities.  
 
These blended perspectives became more evident when I traveled to Singapore and 
experienced cultural differences firsthand. I noticed how discipline, efficiency, and respect for 
rules were deeply embedded in everyday life, which felt different from what I was used to in the 
Philippines. Instead of resisting these differences, I observed and learned from them. As a BSIT 
student, these experiences are valuable because working or migrating abroad is common in my 
field. Understanding different cultures helps me adapt more easily and work better with diverse 
teams. In the future, I can promote cultural empathy by being open- minded, respectful of different 
practices, and considerate when collaborating with people from various backgrounds, especially 
in global or multicultural work environments.

Libut, M ichaela Angela M.               BSIT 2 -B 
 
M1 l Reflective Essay  
 
A defining moment in my life that shaped how I see myself was when I joined a volunteer 
program in my community. I worked with children who didn’t have many opportunities, helping 
them with schoolwork and life skills. At first, it was challenging and somet imes discouraging, but 
I realized that patience, consistency, and genuine effort made a big difference in their lives. From 
this, I learned the meaning of “Pag nag- tanim ng maayos, may bútìd” —if you put in care and 
effort, growth will follow. This philosophy now guides me: small, steady actions lead to 
meaningful results over time. 
Right now, I see myself as hardworking, curious, and determined, but I know I still struggle with 
procrastination and self -doubt. My dreams are to grow in my chosen field, develop my skills, and 
help others along the way. Ten years from now, I hope my future self remembers that growth is a 
process and that rewards come from consistent effort, not instant results. I want to stay patient, 
kind, and focused on the small steps that build long- term success. By embracing challenges and 
learning from mistakes, I can become the confident and capable person I hope to be.  
When I think about my real self and ideal self, I notice that they are not fully aligned yet. I 
am trying to balance ambi tion with patience, learning to trust that steady effort produces real 
results. A moment that showed me this was leading a group project in school, where I had to guide 
my team despite doubts and challenges. By focusing on planning, communication, and effort, I 
was able to help the team succeed and grow alongside them. Experiences like this remind me that 
if I nurture my actions carefully, just like planting seeds, I will eventually see the fruits of my 
work.

M3 Reflective Essay  
My self -perception has been strongly influenced by meaningful social interactions, 
particularly through my role as Vice President of Great Danes Esports, a non -mandated 
organization at AUF. Holding a leadership position allowed me to rediscover my passion for 
helping others and contributing to a shared goal. Through this role, I became more confident as I 
witnessed people placing their trust in me and responding positively to my leadership. The 
organization also encouraged me to become more socially engaged , as collaboration and 
communication were essential to fulfilling my responsibilities. These experiences helped shape 
my identity  and reinforced my understanding of myself as someone capable of growth and 
responsibility within a social group.  
 
In terms of my assumed public image, I believe that many people initially perceive me as 
unapproachable. Based on conversations with my friends, their first impression of me was that I 
appeared “ mataray ” or “ sassy ,” often associated with a serious facial e xpression or my “RBF” 
However, this perception tends to change as people engage in long -term interaction with me. Over 
time, others begin to recognize my extroverted personality and my genuine interest in building 
connections. As a result, I am often able to  form friendships or at least establish familiarity with 
many people beyond their initial judgment.  
 
Feedback from others largely confirmed my assumptions about how I am perceived, 
reinforcing the idea that first impressions do not fully represent a person ’s self -concept. Reflecting 
on this experience through the lens of the Looking -Glass Self , I have come to understand that 
identity is shaped through the interaction between internal traits and external perceptions. My 
extroverted nature plays a significant  role in reshaping how others view me over time. These 
patterns highlight that identity formation is not fixed but continuously developed through social 
interaction. Ultimately, my self -perception has been strengthened by recognizing that sustained 
relatio nships provide a more accurate understanding of who I am than initial appearances.

Libut, Michaela Angela M.								       BSIT 2-B
M5 - Reflective Essay
One of the ways I understand myself better is through my material possessions and the people around me who give meaning to my everyday life. A body part I consider essential to my identity is my hands, because they allow me to express myself through writing, creating, and helping others in simple but meaningful ways. A piece of clothing that represents me is something comfortable yet presentable, reflecting my desire to feel at ease while still showing confidence and self-respect. I also consider a close family member as part of my material world, since their presence continues to influence my values, decisions, and sense of belonging. Alongside these, my phone is one of my most valued possessions because it connects me to people, opportunities, and information that support both my personal and academic life.
As I navigate my digital self, I have learned that the way I present myself online is both a reflection and a selection of who I am. On social media, I would describe myself as expressive but selective, sharing moments that highlight my interests, achievements, and meaningful experiences. While my profiles do represent parts of my real self, they are not entirely complete because I naturally filter out more private struggles or less polished moments. I consciously curate my identity by choosing what to post, how to present it, and how I interact with others, ensuring that my online image aligns with how I want to be perceived. This shows that my digital self is a controlled version of my identity, shaped by both authenticity and intention.
These realizations become more evident when I reflect on the challenges and responsibilities of being active online. I often experience pressures such as comparison with others, the need for validation through likes or comments, and the fear of being judged or misunderstood. Instead of letting these pressures control me, I follow a personal rule of being respectful, mindful, and authentic in my interactions. I remind myself that social media does not always reflect reality, which helps me stay grounded and confident in who I am. Moving forward, I aim to improve my online presence by being more genuine, sharing meaningful reflections, and focusing less on approval while staying true to my real self.

M6 | Reflective Essay
My political and spiritual selves are both shaped by my experiences, environment, and personal reflections. Politically, I see myself as someone who values fairness, accountability, and informed decision-making because these principles help create a more just society. School and media have greatly influenced my political beliefs, especially through lessons about history, governance, and exposure to different viewpoints online. For example, learning about past political events made me realize the importance of active participation and critical thinking. Over time, my beliefs have evolved as I encountered new perspectives and learned to question ideas rather than simply accept them.
My spiritual self is centered on my search for meaning, purpose, and inner peace in my daily life. I believe that spirituality is a personal connection to something greater than myself, expressed through reflection, gratitude, and maintaining strong values. It plays an important role in my decision-making, especially when I face choices that test my integrity and character. There was a time when I had to choose between doing what was easy and what was right, and my spiritual beliefs guided me to act with honesty. That experience strengthened my commitment to living according to my values even when it is difficult.
Family has been the strongest influence on my spiritual identity, as I grew up in an environment where faith and moral values were emphasized. Practices such as prayer and reflection helped shape my perspective and gave me a sense of discipline and direction. These beliefs also help me cope with challenges, as they provide comfort and remind me that difficulties are part of growth. For instance, during times of stress and self-doubt, I turn to reflection and faith to regain strength and clarity. Overall, my political and spiritual selves continue to develop together, guiding how I think, act, and respond to the world around me.
